CPI and PRA for every peripherally exploited core

Source: R/cpi_pra.R
cpi_pra_batch.Rd

Computes the Centripetality Index (CPI) and the Plane-Relative Angle (PRA) of every scar of each core that has an outline, and summarises them per core by their mean and Gini's mean difference (GMD).

Usage

cpi_pra_batch(
  data,
  outlines,
  id_col = "ID",
  start_cols = c("Start_X", "Start_Y", "Start_Z"),
  end_cols = c("End_X", "End_Y", "End_Z"),
  min_length = 0,
  keep = NULL,
  quiet = FALSE
)

Arguments

data

A data frame with one row per scar and the columns named by id_col, start_cols and end_cols. Scars of all cores are stacked.

outlines

A named list with one element per core, named by core ID: the outline points (a three-column matrix or data frame ordered along the loop, as returned by read_outline_iges()) or a plane already fitted with fit_intersection_plane(). Cores without an outline are left out. The outlines must be in the same coordinate frame as the scar columns named by start_cols and end_cols.

id_col

Name of the core ID column. Default "ID".

start_cols, end_cols

Names of the start- and end-point coordinate columns (X, Y, Z). Defaults Start_X/Y/Z and End_X/Y/Z, the columns the scars are recorded in. The aligned columns of align_scar_batch() (s_x... and e_x...) give the same results: these indices do not change when a core is rotated or moved.

min_length

Scars shorter than this (in the units of the coordinates) are left out. Default 0 (keep all). Use it to repeat an analysis without small scars, for example min_length = 10 for 10 mm.

keep

Names of per-core columns (for example "Typology") to carry into the output. Each must be constant within a core.

quiet

Logical. Suppress the summary message? Default FALSE.

Value

A tibble with one row per core that has an outline: the ID column, the keep columns, n_scar (scars used), n_cpi (scars with a defined CPI), CPI_mean, CPI_GMD, PRA_mean, PRA_GMD (degrees), and three checks of the outline: flatness (see fit_intersection_plane()), start_dist (the typical distance of the scar starts from the outline, as a fraction of the outline's size) and frame_ok (start_dist at most 0.03).

Details

The angles. The plane of intersection is fitted to the outline and its centre is the centroid of the enclosed area (see fit_intersection_plane()). CPI is the angle, in the plane, between a scar's removal direction and the direction from the centre to its start: 180 degrees for a scar running towards the centre, 90 for one running along the edge, 0 for one running away from the centre. PRA is the angle between the removal direction and the plane: 0 for a scar running along the plane, 90 for one driven into the core perpendicular to it. PRA does not distinguish the two sides of the plane. Neither angle wraps around, so ordinary means apply.

The core summaries. The mean summarises the overall centripetality or inclination of a core; GMD, the mean absolute difference between the angles of all pairs of its scars, summarises how much they vary. Both are averages over single scars or pairs of scars, so their expectations do not change with the scar count, and they can be compared directly between cores and groups (for example with compare_indices()); the median, interquartile range and standard deviation do not have this property (Xiao et al., in prep.).

When to use. CPI and PRA describe cores flaked from their periphery whose plane of intersection can be identified, such as discoidal and Levallois cores. Supply outlines only for such cores.

The frame check. Scar starts are recorded on the periphery, so they lie on or near the outline when scars and outline share a coordinate frame. start_dist is the median distance of the starts from the outline (over the 85% of starts closest to it) divided by the outline's bounding-box diagonal. Cores whose start_dist exceeds 0.03 are flagged with a warning: their scars and outline are probably in different frames or units, and their angles are not meaningful. Use plot_core() to look.

Rows with missing coordinates or zero length, and scars shorter than min_length, are left out. Cores with fewer than three usable scars get NA. A scar whose start lies on the centre, or which runs exactly along the normal, has no CPI; n_cpi counts the scars that have one.

References

Gini, C. (1912). Variabilità e mutabilità. Bologna: C. Cuppini.

Yitzhaki, S. (2003). Gini's mean difference: a superior measure of variability for non-normal distributions. Metron, 61(2), 285–316.

See also

read_outline_iges(), fit_intersection_plane(), cpi_pra_per_scar(), plot_core(), spi_ei_batch()

Examples

# A disc-shaped core: twelve scars from the edge towards the centre
t <- seq(0, 2 * pi, length.out = 13)[-13]
start <- cbind(30 * cos(t), 30 * sin(t), 0)
end <- start * 0.4
end[, 3] <- -5
scars <- data.frame(ID = "disc", Start_X = start[, 1], Start_Y = start[, 2],
                    Start_Z = start[, 3], End_X = end[, 1], End_Y = end[, 2],
                    End_Z = end[, 3])
u <- seq(0, 2 * pi, length.out = 200)
outlines <- list(disc = cbind(30 * cos(u), 30 * sin(u), 0))
cpi_pra_batch(scars, outlines)
#> Warning: Outline of core disc: collapsing to unique 'x' values
#> Warning: Outline of core disc: collapsing to unique 'x' values
#> Warning: Outline of core disc: collapsing to unique 'x' values
#> CPI and PRA computed for 1 core(s) with an outline.

#>   ID    n_scar n_cpi CPI_mean CPI_GMD PRA_mean  PRA_GMD flatness start_dist
#>   <chr>  <int> <int>    <dbl>   <dbl>    <dbl>    <dbl>    <dbl>      <dbl>
#> 1 disc      12    12      180       0     15.5 2.80e-15        0  0.0000288
